skill.name: design-mobile-apps
skill.description: Design mobile interfaces with Sleek, review generated screens, and implement approved designs in HTML, React Native, or SwiftUI.
skill.summary: Design, review, and implement mobile app screens through the Sleek API.
skill.author: designed-by-ai

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholder credentials, example URLs, and API documentation rather than executable shell syntax. The skill has intentional network access, while semantic review found unsafe conversational key handling, an inaccurate host boundary, and unvalidated external HTML.

remediation.issue: The fallback asks users to paste a newly created API key into chat.
remediation.suggestion: Use device authorization only. Never request raw keys in conversation; store returned credentials in a local secret manager with explicit user consent.

remediation.issue: The declared sleek.design-only network boundary conflicts with required Iconify downloads.
remediation.suggestion: Declare every required host and data flow, or remove third-party requests by obtaining vetted assets through the declared service.

remediation.issue: Complete external HTML may include active scripts and is saved without a validation step.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect and sanitize generated HTML before saving or opening it. Remove remote scripts and use locally vetted static assets.

content.user_title: Design and Implement Mobile App Interfaces
content.value_statement: Mobile app concepts often lack a coherent visual direction and implementation-ready details. This skill generates, reviews, and translates Sleek screens into working interfaces.
actual_capabilities: Creates Sleek projects and sends design briefs through the REST API.
Generates new mobile screens or targets existing screens for revisions.
Polls asynchronous design runs and reports completion or failure.
Renders viewport and full-height screenshots for presentation and review.
Retrieves versioned component HTML, including explicitly pinned versions.
Guides translation of generated HTML into React Native, SwiftUI, or HTML.
limitations: Requires network access and a scoped Sleek API key.
Generations consume credits, and sustained use may require a paid plan.
Results depend on the availability and output quality of the external Sleek service.
Native implementation still requires framework-specific adaptation and testing.

use_cases.title: Explore a New Product
use_cases.description: Turn a product brief into coordinated mobile screens with a defined visual direction.

use_cases.title: Review Interface Variations
use_cases.description: Create separate design directions, compare screenshots, and refine the selected option.

use_cases.title: Implement Approved Screens
use_cases.description: Retrieve component HTML and screenshots as references for a native application implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mobile welcome screen for [product]. Include [content] and use a [mood] visual direction.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs one screen from a short brief.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Core Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the [flow] for [audience]. Include [screens], preserve [brand requirements], and show screenshots of every generated screen.
prompt_templates.scenario: A product team needs a connected group of screens.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Update screen [screen name] in project [project]. Improve [specific issue] while preserving [elements]. Review the full-height result before reporting completion.
prompt_templates.scenario: An existing Sleek project needs a targeted revision.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Native Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the approved screens in [framework]. Fetch active component HTML, preserve exact icons and fonts, then verify navigation and layout against screenshots.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs an implementation based on approved designs.

output_examples.input: Design an onboarding flow for a personal budgeting application.
output: Created a project with welcome, goals, account connection, and completion screens.
Applied a calm financial style with clear progress and restrained color.
Presented viewport screenshots and reviewed full-height captures.

output_examples.input: Make the existing activity screen easier to scan during workouts.
output_examples.output: Updated the targeted screen with stronger hierarchy, larger metrics, clearer controls, and preserved navigation. Presented the revised screenshot for review.

output_examples.input: Implement the approved profile screen in React Native.
output_examples.output: Retrieved the active component version and visual reference. Recreated the structure, typography, icons, imagery, and navigation for React Native.

best_practices: Provide product goals, audience, required screens, references, and constraints before generation.
Use scoped, revocable credentials and confirm any action that may consume credits or remove data.
Review full-height screenshots before requesting corrections, then verify native implementations against viewport screenshots.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into prompts, chat messages, source files, or generated outputs.
Do not judge missing content from viewport screenshots without checking a full-height capture.
Do not substitute icons, fonts, screen identifiers, or component versions without confirming the change.

faq.question: What is required to use this skill?
faq.answer: You need network access, a Sleek account, and an API key with scopes appropriate for the task.

faq.question: Can it create several screens?
faq.answer: Yes. A single design request can produce a coordinated flow with multiple screens.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing Sleek project?
faq.answer: Yes. It can target an existing screen when you provide the project and screen context.

faq.question: Does it support native mobile frameworks?
faq.answer: It provides HTML and screenshots as references for React Native, SwiftUI, and other native implementations.

faq.question: Does it require a paid Sleek plan?
faq.answer: Trial credits may support an initial design. Continued generation can require a paid plan.

faq.question: How should generated screens be reviewed?
faq.answer: Use viewport screenshots for presentation and full-height screenshots for completeness checks. Inspect component HTML when a negative visual conclusion remains uncertain.
